CRESPO, SR Secretary to the Mayor Municipality of Patnongon Province of Antique Dear Mr. Crespo, Sr.: This pertains to your Letter dated December 12, 2024, requesting this Department's opinion on whether a local chief executive (LCE) may be penalized for implementing an executive order that has not been reviewed by the reviewing authority pursuant to Sections 30 and 468 of Republic Act 7160, or the Local Government Code, hereinafter referred to as the "Code." This Department is of the opinion that an LCE may not be penalized for implementing an EO that has not undergone review by the appropriate reviewing authority. To bolster this, the Code does not explicitly impose penalties on an LCE for implementing an EO sans prior review by the reviewing authority (i.e., the governor for EOS promulgated by the component city or municipality; the city or municipal mayor for EOS promulgated by the punong barangay within his jurisdiction). Along this line, it is important to note that the Code empowers the LCE to issue EOS to operationalize and implement ordinances within his jurisdiction. However, this power must be exercised within the bounds of law; it is not absolute. It must not run contrary to existing laws, ordinances, and public policy. What the law specifically provides is the review mechanism, which fundamentally operates as a post-facto check to ascertain that the EO promulgated is not inconsistent with legal and regulatory requirements. Section 30 of the Code, provides: "Section 30. Review of Executive Orders. - (a) Except as otherwise provided under the Constitution and special statutes, the governor shall review all executive orders promulgated by the component city or municipal mayor within his jurisdiction. The city or municipal mayor shall review all executive orders promulgated by the punong barangay within his jurisdiction. Copies of such orders shall be forwarded to the governor or the city or municipal mayor, as the case may be, within three (3) days from their issuance. In all instances of review, the local chief executive concerned shall ensure that such executive orders are within the powers granted by law and in conformity with provincial, city, or municipal ordinances. executive orders are within the powers granted by law and in conformity with provincial, city, or municipal ordinances. (b) If the governor or the city or municipal mayor fails to act on said executive orders within thirty (30) days after their submission, the same shall be deemed consistent with law and therefore valid." Here, it bears noting that the Code does not expressly require prior review of an EO before it can be implemented. Accordingly, this Department is of the submission that pending review by the appropriate reviewing authority, the EO can be validly enforced. As long as the procedural requirements for the promulgation of an EO have been complied with, then the shall same already be given full force and effect. Notwithstanding, please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. ROMEO . BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA'RPBJLLLS-LRALLD0am JUAN JOVIAN E.
